orchestrator/skills_registry.py:267 dependency_hashes() applies to every discovered/quarantined skill on every sync() (see the discovered.json loop that calls dependency_hashes(source, dependencies, repo=...) using the skill's own frontmatter depends_on list). Declarations may be absolute paths (candidate.is_absolute(): if candidate.is_file(): paths.add(candidate)) or globs resolved with no repo/quarantine containment check. An external, still-quarantined and uninspected skill can therefore declare depends_on: ['/etc/passwd','/Users/<user>/.ssh/id_rsa', ...] and the orchestrator will read and sha256-hash those files and store {absolute_path: hash} in the skill's registry record before any human review or inspect gate runs, and that record is later exposed via `orchestrator skills show <id> --json`/`skills list`. That's an arbitrary-file existence/fingerprint disclosure primitive driven entirely by untrusted skill submission content, which is exactly the trust boundary this review is meant to check (external content must not gain filesystem reach it wasn't granted). It should restrict depends_on resolution for non-builtin/quarantined skills to paths inside the skill's own quarantine directory (mirroring the containment check already done for provenance!='builtin' in skill_promotion._inspection).

Planner note: both comments are right; the first is a trust-boundary bug. (1) dependency_hashes() must only resolve paths INSIDE the repository root (builtins) or inside the skill's own quarantine directory (external/learned records); absolute paths, parent traversal and globs that escape those roots are ignored and recorded as "dependency_ignored" in history; hashing never runs for records in state discovered or quarantined until they reach testing. (2) Add the missing registry tests to SkillsRegistryTests: test_dependency_hashes_never_escape_repo_or_quarantine (an absolute path and a ../ glob in an external record's depends_on are ignored, nothing outside is read: assert with a sentinel file outside the roots), test_sync_marks_stale_on_dependency_change, test_revalidate_clears_stale_on_success, test_rollback_skips_noop_transitions, test_drafts_are_redacted_on_write.

result.summary: Fix-round commit a212a5f in wt/T-0980 confines dependency_hashes() to the repo root (builtin) or the skill's own quarantine directory (external/learned), rejecting absolute paths, '..' traversal, and symlink escapes (resolve() runs before the containment check), and skips hashing entirely for discovered/quarantined records via the new _record_dependency_hashes gate. This resolves the arbitrary-file-read trust boundary comment. The missing SkillsRegistryTests coverage was also added: test_dependency_hashes_never_escape_repo_or_quarantine, test_sync_marks_stale_on_dependency_change, and test_revalidate_clears_stale_on_success are present as real unittest.TestCase methods (plus bonus tests for rollback no-op and draft redaction). Ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_skills_registry.py` directly: all 14 tests pass, including the three required new ones. Both original rejecting review comments are addressed and all listed acceptance criteria are satisfied.
